story: A UAA-led NSF EPSCoR award of about $6 million across Alaska, Montana and Wyoming will pair microbes with AI to try to recover rare earth elements from coal refuse and ash

claims.claim: NSF award 2614749 went to the University of Alaska Anchorage.
claims.verbatim: "awardeeName":"University of Alaska Anchorage Campus"
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation award database
claims.notes: Location is the awardeeName field of the NSF API record. The award date of August 5th falls before the September 28th window, so the record is background. The in-window news peg is UAF News on October 5th (C17).

claims.claim: Brandon Briggs is the principal investigator on the UAA award.
claims.verbatim: "piFirstName":"Brandon"
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation award database
claims.notes: The adjacent field reads "piLastName":"Briggs". UAA News (January 22nd, background) calls him "Brandon Briggs, Ph.D., professor of biological sciences".

claims.claim: The UAA award carries an estimated total of $3,824,575.
claims.verbatim: "estimatedTotalAmt":"3824575"
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation award database
claims.notes: fundsObligatedAmt is also 3824575. This is the largest of the three linked awards. The three records sum to $5,998,412, which matches UAF's "$6 million" (C17).

claims.claim: NSF dated the UAA award August 5th.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation award database
claims.notes: BACKGROUND because it falls outside the window. The awards for UAF (2614751) and Montana Tech (2614750) carry the same date.

claims.claim: The award period begins September 1st.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation award database
claims.notes: The same start date appears on 2614750 and 2614751.

claims.claim: The award period ends August 31st, 2030, making it a four-year project.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation award database
claims.notes: The NSF OIA announcement independently says "These four-year projects are designed to build lasting research partnerships".

claims.claim: The award is funded through the NSF EPSCoR Focused EPSCoR Collaborations track.
claims.verbatim: "EPSCoR RII: Focused EPSCoR Col"
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation award database
claims.notes: The API truncates the fundProgramName field. The full name, "Focused EPSCoR Collaborations (FEC)", is confirmed on the NSF OIA announcement page.

claims.claim: The three linked NSF awards share the project title Transformative Bioprocessing and AI-Driven Frameworks for Sustainable Critical Mineral Recovery.
claims.verbatim: Collaborative Research: FEC: Transformative Bioprocessing and AI-Driven Frameworks for Sustainable Critical Mineral Recovery
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation award database
claims.notes: The identical title appears on 2614749 and 2614750 and on the NSF OIA announcement. The claim drops the "Collaborative Research FEC" prefix because house rules bar colons in claim text.

claims.claim: NSF award 2614751 went to the University of Alaska Fairbanks.
claims.verbatim: University of Alaska Fairbanks Campus
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation award database
claims.notes: Location is the awardeeName field of record 2614751.

claims.claim: The UAF award is $913,037.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation award database
claims.notes: The value appears in both fundsObligatedAmt and estimatedTotalAmt. UAF News independently says UAF's portion is "supported by nearly $913,000 of the total award".

claims.claim: Srijan Aggarwal, a UAF professor of environmental engineering, leads UAF's portion as a principal investigator.
claims.verbatim: Srijan Aggarwal, UAF professor of environmental engineering and a principal investigator
claims.source_outlet: UAF News, University of Alaska Fairbanks
claims.notes: NSF record 2614751 independently lists piFirstName Srijan and piLastName Aggarwal. UAF is an awardee, so its news release counts as the institution's own statement.

claims.claim: NSF award 2614750 gives Montana Technological University $1,260,800.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation award database
claims.notes: The value appears in fundsObligatedAmt and estimatedTotalAmt. awardeeName reads "Montana Technological University".

claims.claim: Robin Bullock is the principal investigator on the Montana Tech award.
claims.verbatim: Bullock
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation award database
claims.notes: Location is the piLastName field. piFirstName reads "Robin".

claims.claim: The award abstract says UAA leads the project in partnership with UAF, Montana Technological University and the University of Wyoming.
claims.verbatim: in partnership with the University of Alaska Fairbanks, Montana Technological University, and the University of Wyoming
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation award database
claims.notes: From abstractText. UAF News names the same four institutions.

claims.claim: NSF lists the University of Wyoming as a subawardee on the project.
claims.verbatim: University of Alaska Fairbanks Campus, Subawardee: University of Wyoming
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation, Office of Integrative Activities
claims.notes: BACKGROUND (August 24th). This explains why Wyoming has no award record of its own. The page does not say which lead award carries the subaward.

claims.claim: The UAA award lists four co-principal investigators, one of them Tyler C Brown with a University of Wyoming email address.
claims.verbatim: Tyler C Brown tbrown46@uwyo.edu
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation award database
claims.notes: The other three coPDPI entries are "Mohammad Heidari Kapourchali mhkapourchali@alaska.edu", "Subhabrata Dev sdev@alaska.edu" and "Masoumeh Heidari Kapourchali mheidari2@alaska.edu". An alaska.edu address does not show which campus, so do not call those three UAA faculty.

claims.claim: UAF describes the project as a $6 million NSF-funded effort.
claims.verbatim: The $6 million National Science Foundation-funded project
claims.source_outlet: UAF News, University of Alaska Fairbanks
claims.notes: Sanity check passed. 3,824,575 plus 913,037 plus 1,260,800 equals 5,998,412. This is the in-window news peg (October 5th).

claims.claim: UAF's share of the work sits at its Institute of Northern Engineering.
claims.verbatim: Researchers at the University of Alaska Fairbanks Institute of Northern Engineering
claims.source_outlet: UAF News, University of Alaska Fairbanks
claims.notes: Taken from the opening of the release.

claims.claim: The project aims to recover rare earth elements from domestic coal refuse and ash using microbes.
claims.verbatim: transform microbial rare earth element (REE) recovery from domestic coal refuse and ash into a predictive
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation award database
claims.notes: This is a plan, not a result. Phrase it as "aims to" or "plans to". UAF News corroborates with "can help recover rare earth elements from coal refuse and ash".

claims.claim: The abstract plans a predictive Virtual Assay to screen feedstocks.
claims.verbatim: predictive Virtual Assay to screen feedstocks
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation award database
claims.notes: Prospective. Write "will build" or "plans", not "uses".

claims.claim: The abstract plans reinforcement-learning controllers inside a bioprocess digital twin linked to microgrid simulators.
claims.verbatim: reinforcement-learning controllers within a bioprocess digital twin integrated with microgrid simulators
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation award database
claims.notes: This is the core AI element, and it is prospective.

claims.claim: The project will test extraction by the bacterium Shewanella oneidensis against techno-economic and life-cycle metrics.
claims.verbatim: Shewanella oneidensis extraction performance against techno-economic and life-cycle performance metrics
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation award database
claims.notes: Prospective. The organism is named in the abstract only. Calling Shewanella a bacterium is general knowledge, not page text.

claims.claim: The abstract frames the goal as a predictive, energy-constrained system.
claims.verbatim: a predictive, energy-constrained system
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation award database
claims.notes: Ties to the Alaska angle. Aggarwal says in UAF News that Alaska's remote energy challenges make energy use central.

claims.claim: The abstract names a Smart Bio-Refinery framework and a Virtual Pilot Plant as project outputs.
claims.verbatim: Smart Bio-Refinery framework and Virtual Pilot Plant
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation award database
claims.notes: UAF News says "A virtual pilot plant will connect experimental results with computer models" and uses the phrase "smart bio-refinery". The NSF OIA page says the project "establishes a Smart Bio-Refinery framework". Prospective.

claims.claim: The abstract plans a federally compliant University Recharge Facility.
claims.verbatim: establishing a federally compliant University Recharge Facility
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation award database
claims.notes: Prospective. The abstract text fetched does not say which campus hosts it, so don't name one.

claims.claim: Workforce plans include industry-aligned micro-credentials and a Tri-State Field Course.
claims.verbatim: industry-aligned micro-credentials, and a Tri-State Field Course
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation award database
claims.notes: Prospective. UAF News also lists microcredentials, an early-career leadership council and a tri-state field course.

claims.claim: The award abstract says the U.S. relies heavily on foreign sources for rare earth elements.
claims.verbatim: The U.S. relies heavily on foreign sources for rare earth elements (REEs)
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation award database
claims.notes: This is the applicants' motivating framing, so attribute it ("the award abstract says"). UAF News echoes it with "reduce reliance on foreign sources". No import share figure was verified, so don't add one.

claims.claim: UAF says AI will help predict how readily rare earth elements can be recovered from different materials.
claims.verbatim: predicting how readily rare earth elements can be recovered from different materials
claims.source_outlet: UAF News, University of Alaska Fairbanks
claims.notes: Prospective. Say "is expected to" or "will be used to". This is the plain-language version of the Virtual Assay (C20).

claims.claim: UAF says the team will develop controls that adjust bioreactor operation as conditions and energy availability change.
claims.verbatim: developing controls that adjust bioreactor operation as conditions and energy availability change
claims.source_outlet: UAF News, University of Alaska Fairbanks
claims.notes: Prospective. This is the plain-language version of C21.

claims.claim: The project is one of eight NSF EPSCoR projects sharing a combined $39.9 million.
claims.verbatim: one of eight projects receiving a combined $39.9 million
claims.source_outlet: UAF News, University of Alaska Fairbanks
claims.notes: Independently confirmed by the NSF OIA announcement (C33, C34).

claims.claim: UAF says this EPSCoR award is separate from, and in addition to, NSF support for the UAF-led Critical Mineral Accelerator Engine.
claims.verbatim: This EPSCoR award is in addition to NSF's support for the UAF-led NSF Critical Mineral Accelerator Engine in Alaska.
claims.source_outlet: UAF News, University of Alaska Fairbanks
claims.notes: The page has a typographic apostrophe in NSF's, normalized here to straight. The page wording is "in addition to", not "separate". Keep the two efforts distinct on the slides.

claims.claim: Aggarwal said "This collaboration brings together expertise that no single institution could provide on its own."
claims.verbatim: This collaboration brings together expertise that no single institution could provide on its own
claims.source_outlet: UAF News, University of Alaska Fairbanks
claims.notes: The quote by a named person is verbatim on the page. The quote has no internal apostrophes.

claims.claim: Aggarwal said "We're connecting environmental engineering, microbiology, mineral processing and AI."
claims.value: environmental engineering, microbiology, mineral processing and AI
claims.verbatim: We're connecting environmental engineering, microbiology, mineral processing and AI
claims.source_outlet: UAF News, University of Alaska Fairbanks
claims.notes: Verbatim. The fetch reported a straight apostrophe in "We're" on the page. The sentence continues "to recover valuable elements from materials left behind as waste."

claims.claim: NSF announced $39.9 million in EPSCoR Focused EPSCoR Collaborations awards in August.
claims.verbatim: is investing $39.9 million through its Established Program
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation, Office of Integrative Activities
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. The announcement is dated August 24th, which is outside the window. The page renders $39.9 in bold, and the markup is stripped here.

claims.claim: The eight awards span research teams in 16 NSF EPSCoR jurisdictions.
claims.verbatim: The eight awards will support research teams working across 16 NSF EPSCoR jurisdictions
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation, Office of Integrative Activities
claims.notes: BACKGROUND (August 24th).

claims.claim: Coal used in UAA's earlier rare-earth biomining research was donated by Usibelli Coal Mine in Healy.
claims.verbatim: The ores Gleason used were coal samples donated by Usibelli Coal Mine in Healy.
claims.source_outlet: UAA News, University of Alaska Anchorage
claims.notes: BACKGROUND (January 22nd, by Keenan James Britt). The same text is in the UAA Alumni Spirit magazine copy (Spring/Summer 2026). This article does not mention NSF, AI or the new award, so present it as earlier lab work and not as part of the award.

claims.claim: A UAA graduate researcher said Usibelli coal has relatively high concentrations of rare earth elements, including scandium and yttrium.
claims.verbatim: Gleason noted that Usibelli coal "has relatively high concentrations of REEs" including scandium and yttrium.
claims.source_outlet: UAA News, University of Alaska Anchorage
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. This is D'Lynn Gleason's characterization, with no concentration figure given. Attribute it ("according to UAA researcher D'Lynn Gleason").

claims.claim: Gleason said Alaska does not currently mine rare earth elements.
claims.verbatim: we don't currently have mining here for rare-earth elements
claims.source_outlet: UAA News, University of Alaska Anchorage
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. This is a quote from D'Lynn Gleason ("Alaska has a lot of rich mineral sources [but] we don't currently have mining here for rare-earth elements."). Attribute it to her and do not state it as the deck's own finding.

claims.claim: Gleason said the coal's rare earths sit at concentrations too small to mine with acid efficiently.
claims.verbatim: We can't traditionally mine them with acid, because they're just at such small concentrations that it wouldn't be feasible or wouldn't be efficient.
claims.source_outlet: UAA News, University of Alaska Anchorage
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. The fetch returned this verbatim quote from D'Lynn Gleason as two adjacent pieces, joined here. Attribute it.

claims.claim: Bacteria for the earlier UAA thesis came from Kennicott Glacier and Root Glacier in Wrangell-St. Elias National Park.
claims.verbatim: Kennicott Glacier and Root Glacier in Wrangell-St. Elias National Park
claims.source_outlet: UAA News, University of Alaska Anchorage
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. The thesis is titled "Binding Activity of Glacier Bacteria Towards Rare Earth Elements" (verbatim on page). The samples were collected by "a team led by Brandon Briggs, Ph.D., professor of biological sciences, during a June 2022 trip".

claims.claim: The separate UAF-led NSF Critical Mineral Accelerator Engine receives $15 million in its first two years.
claims.verbatim: will receive $15 million during its first two years
claims.source_outlet: UAF Geophysical Institute
claims.notes: BACKGROUND (July 14th, Rod Boyce). The page says "It is led by Lee Ann Munk of the UAF Geophysical Institute." Alaska Public Media/KUAC (September 23rd) also confirms "$15 million this summer".

claims.claim: The Engine could receive up to $160 million over 10 years.
claims.verbatim: could receive up to $160 million over 10 years
claims.source_outlet: UAF Geophysical Institute
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. This is a ceiling, not an award, so use "up to" or "could". Alaska Public Media writes "an additional $160 million", which conflicts with the GI wording. Use the GI wording, which is primary.

claims.claim: The Engine plans to use artificial intelligence to help locate mineral deposits.
claims.verbatim: It will also use artificial intelligence to help locate mineral deposits
claims.source_outlet: UAF Geophysical Institute
claims.notes: BACKGROUND and prospective. Contrast with the EPSCoR project, which applies AI to recovery from waste rather than to finding deposits.

claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation
claims.notes: Program title on page is "U.S. National Science Foundation State and Regional Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure Hubs".

claims.story: NSF 26-513 State and Regional AI Infrastructure Hubs

claims.verbatim: request 5 years and between $4,000,000 - $12,000,000 total budget.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation

claims.story: NSF 26-513 State and Regional AI Infrastructure Hubs
claims.claim: NSF estimates 10 hub awards.
claims.verbatim: Estimated Number of Awards: 10
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation
claims.notes: This is an estimate, so write "about 10" or "an estimated 10".

claims.story: NSF 26-513 State and Regional AI Infrastructure Hubs
claims.claim: The first full proposal deadline is November 4th.
claims.verbatim: November 04, 2026
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation
claims.notes: The next deadline is November 3rd, 2027, and then "First Wednesday in November, Annually Thereafter".

claims.story: NSF 26-513 State and Regional AI Infrastructure Hubs
claims.claim: NSF last updated the solicitation page on October 5th.
claims.verbatim: Last updated: October 5, 2026
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation

claims.story: NSF 26-513 State and Regional AI Infrastructure Hubs
claims.claim: NSF award 2433241, Rural AI Solutions and Engagement (RAISE), gives the University of Alaska Anchorage $380,000.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation award database

The title reads "Collaborative Research: EPIIC: Rural AI Solutions and Engagement (RAISE)" and the awardee is "University of Alaska Anchorage Campus".

claims.story: NSF 26-513 State and Regional AI Infrastructure Hubs

claims.verbatim: Mock
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation award database
claims.notes: Location is the piLastName field. piFirstName reads "Kenrick". The UAA coeng page does not name him.

claims.claim: UAA's Alaska AI Solutions Consortium set October 7th as the full proposal deadline for its RAISE community partner mini grants.
claims.verbatim: Full Proposal: October 7, 2026
claims.source_outlet: UAA College of Engineering, Artificial Intelligence @ UAA
claims.notes: The page is undated. Its title is "RAISE Mini Grants – 2026 Community Partner Call" and it says "The Alaska AI Solutions Consortium (AISC)" and "Funded by the NSF under Award #2433241". The deadline is in the window.

claims.story: NSF 26-513 State and Regional AI Infrastructure Hubs
claims.claim: RAISE mini grant awards are to be announced November 2nd.
claims.verbatim: Award Announcement: November 2, 2026
claims.source_outlet: UAA College of Engineering, Artificial Intelligence @ UAA

killed.claim: Goldschmidt 2023 abstract by Briggs and Martinez on Shewanella oneidensis bioreactors with US coals
killed.why: PDF, showrunner to fetch. https://goldschmidtabstracts.info/2023/18997.pdf returned compressed PDF data. The only readable metadata title was "Circum-neutral Weathering of REE Containing Minerals", and Shewanella, coal and the author names did not appear in the readable text.

killed.claim: The Alaska Public Media article names Pogo mine tailings as a critical mineral source
killed.why: Not found on the fetched page.

killed.claim: The Engine project is working on Red Dog mine tailings
killed.why: The only fragment is "They're already trying to do that at the Red Dog zinc mine in northwestern Alaska". It is unclear what "that" refers to, and the page does not mention AI. Too ambiguous to use.

killed.claim: The Engine will receive an additional $160 million over the next decade (Alaska Public Media wording)
killed.why: Conflicts with the primary UAF Geophysical Institute wording "could receive up to $160 million over 10 years". The primary version is kept as C42.

killed.claim: UAA published its own news item about award 2614749
killed.why: None was found on the UAA news homepage or the first page of the UAA research news archive. The only institutional release is UAF's.

killed.claim: UAA's earlier glacier-bacteria biomining thesis is part of the NSF award
killed.why: The January 22nd UAA article mentions neither NSF nor AI. Use it only as background on Briggs's lab, never as part of the award.

killed.claim: Rare earth elements are a group of 17 transition metals
killed.why: The page does say it ("a group of 17 transition metals"), but the classification is loose because most rare earths are lanthanides. Not needed for the deck. If 17 is used, say "17 elements" and cite general knowledge, not this page.

killed.claim: The UAF News page says the project is "separate" from the Engine
killed.why: The word "separate" does not appear. The page says "in addition to". Reworded as C31.

killed.claim: The UAA coeng RAISE page names Kenrick Mock
killed.why: His name is not on that page. The PI is verified from the NSF award record instead (C50).

killed.claim: UAA's RAISE consortium is positioning for an NSF 26-513 AI Infrastructure Hub bid
killed.why: No fetched page connects RAISE or AISC to solicitation 26-513. Any link is the scout's inference, so the two can sit side by side only as separate facts.

killed.claim: APD says no police report was filed over the downed Flock camera
killed.why: KTUU's subheadline and URL say no report was filed, but its body says "APD confirmed Lowe's filed a report". The source contradicts itself, so use neither framing about the report beyond the body's attributed account.

killed.claim: Lowe's retention of 90 days is Flock's policy
killed.why: The ADN context shows the 90-day figure comes from Lowe's privacy statement, not Flock's. Kept only as Lowe's (C55).
